paper.title: Hierarchical Floorplan-Guided Vision-Language Exploration for Embodied Question Answering
paper.central_claim: HFLEX-EQA combines an online hierarchical scene graph, a VLM high-level planner that selects among explore_room / go_to_objects / find_room, specialized low-level planners and a topological floorplan prior for room discovery, and outperforms GraphEQA and ExploreEQA on OpenEQA and ExploreEQA across five VLMs, with deployment on a quadruped robot.
paper.claim_scope_note: Evaluation is restricted to single-floor HM3D episodes with semantic annotations (108 + 114); the simulated floorplan is generated from HM3D semantic annotations and the real one is built manually; 'SOTA' is relative to two re-run baselines.

sections_read: V Experiments A-C (Tables I-IV, Figs 4-5 captions)

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: Hydra scene graph + open-vocabulary occupancy map; a frozen VLM gets the serialized scene graph, CLIP-selected key views, decision history and a floorplan graph and returns a mode, target, optional answer and confidence (answer accepted when confidence >= 0.8); low-level planners score frontiers (CLIP similarity), sample visibility-maximizing viewpoints, or weight frontiers by floorplan shortest-path distance to the target room class. Evidence: five VLMs x two datasets with re-run baselines under a 50-iteration budget; SRs are integer counts of 108/114 (single run, no CI); multiple-choice success is exact, no-choice success is graded by an unaudited LLM. Gemini-only ablations: removing the floorplan drops 75.0 -> 64.8 (OpenEQA) and 63.2 -> 53.5 (ExploreEQA); without the floorplan HFLEX is 53.5 on ExploreEQA vs GraphEQA 54.4, so the ExploreEQA advantage depends on the floorplan, which is derived from ground-truth annotations and not given to baselines (GraphEQA+FP prompt control: 43.5 / 57.0). Real world: Table IV 'representative question types', 7 episodes once each, all correct, no statement of total attempts; no-choice and perturbation results are replays. Initial view: solid same-VLM simulated comparison with useful ablations; information asymmetry, single runs and a selected real-world table limit the claims.

evidence.support_explanation: Nearest explicit ancestor; claims not fresh invention of scene-graph memory.

evidence.quote: In our experiments, we construct \mathcal{G}^{\mathcal{F}} from HM3D [ 23 ] semantic annotations in simulation and manually from known room layouts in the real world.
evidence.support_explanation: Global unseen-room prior is exogenous, privileged relative to purely online RGB-D baselines, not inferred from observations.

evidence.quote: Metric geometry and agent localization are not retained.
evidence.support_explanation: Privilege does not include exact geometry/localization; avoid overstating.

evidence.quote: For each room, at most M key views are selected

evidence.quote: We constrain the VLM to only predict classes present in the floorplan
evidence.support_explanation: Missing floorplan class can bias observed-room classification; perturbation robustness not topology robustness.

evidence.quote: If an answer a_{t} is provided with confidence \kappa_{t}\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{min}} , it is returned as the final answer and the episode terminates.
evidence.support_explanation: VLM self-confidence stop, not externally validated EQA answer gate.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Simulated closed-loop EQA with exact multiple-choice success over 108/114 episodes. Transfer withheld: the seven real-world episodes are labelled 'representative', run once each with no stated total of attempts (not a counted trial protocol), use a hand-built floorplan of the deployment site, and the free-form results are replays; sim evaluation uses HM3D only.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 108 OpenEQA / 114 ExploreEQA single-floor HM3D episodes, with the same VLM and 50-iteration cap, HFLEX-EQA's multiple-choice SR exceeds re-run GraphEQA/ExploreEQA for all five VLMs (single runs). In the Gemini ablation the hierarchy without the floorplan still leads on OpenEQA (64.8 vs 46.3) but not on ExploreEQA (53.5 vs 54.4), where the gain depends on the annotation-derived floorplan.
not_supported_as_stated: state of the art beyond the two re-run baselines
assessment.not_claimed: No reproduction; all results are author reports.

G.reason: Concrete residual after GraphEQA (single planning strategy, unused structural priors) with nearest neighbours named and re-run; the 'weak prior' premise is not tested. Both seats agree.

M.reason: Mode selection by missing-information type plus topology-distance weighting is reconstructible with distinguishable predictions (FP removal hurts; naive prompting with the floorplan does not); behaviour under noisy floorplans is the untested core assumption. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Equations 3-14 and all weights/thresholds given; prompts, graph serialization details and parameter-selection data missing; failure boundary for erroneous floorplans untested. Both seats agree.

measurement.reason: Anchors v2 'criterion exists but denominators incomplete -> 2': multiple-choice success is exact with 108/114 denominators, but half of the simulated results (no-choice) are graded by an unaudited LLM judge (EVIDENCE rule 3) and the real-world results are seven 'representative' single runs without a total-attempt denominator.

causality.reason: Same-VLM re-run baselines across five VLMs, leave-one-out removals, GraphEQA+FP information control and GT-semantics analysis separate most explanations; remaining: single-run Gemini-only ablations and the floorplan being extra annotation-derived information, which carries the whole ExploreEQA advantage (agg:E001). Both seats agree at 3.

holdout.reason: No training, but the floorplan is derived from HM3D ground-truth annotations / hand-built, evaluation is restricted to episodes where it can be generated, no erroneous-floorplan test, hyperparameter selection data unstated; real runs are representative single episodes. Anchors precedent 1 direction (privileged-information channel deducts holdout). Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Anchors v2: single run, no variance/CI, no failure breakdown -> <=1. Both seats agree.

cost.reason: Matched 50-iteration cap and per-method planning steps and path length (physical cost) reported; internal VLM call counts inferable only roughly, tokens/latency/USD missing and the floorplan channel unpriced. Matches anchor 2 ('budget inferable, privileged channel unpriced'), above 1.

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE.md transfer needs counted closed-loop trials in a construction-unused setting; Table IV is labelled 'representative question types' with one execution each and no stated total of attempts, the deployment floorplan is hand-built from the site's known layout, and free-form results are replays. Unlike 2609.39915 (explicit 8 routes x 3 trials), no trial protocol is stated.

son55_value.reason: 完整 HTML 全文；无独立附录；Fig 5 数值仅在图中。

resolutions.reason: C25 is executed: the VLM emits a typed (mode, target, answer, confidence) artifact, deterministic planners execute, fresh observations and the updated scene graph return each iteration, and terminal-answer confidence (explicitly listed in C25) gates answering. Missing feedback-gate ablation is a failed success condition, not absence of the tactic. Same rule as 2609.39915 (loop present -> C25) vs 2503.02465/2512.10394 (no loop -> null).

The mode split by missing-information type is already the primary decomposition (routing sub-problems to specialized planners), so a heterogeneous_decomposition supporting card duplicates it. The floorplan contribution is a distinct operation: room-adjacency topology and its shortest-path statistic are baked into the frontier-scoring operator rather than left to the VLM (GraphEQA+FP shows prompting alone does not help), which is C13's relational-topology instantiation; partial because it is a soft weight, not a by-construction guarantee.

Anchors v2 partial-denominator clause: the real-world results lack a total-attempt denominator, and the no-choice half of the simulated results relies on an unaudited LLM grader (EVIDENCE rule 3). son55's 3 lists both gaps but did not apply the v2 clause.

Matched iteration cap plus per-method steps and path length is more than 'proxies only'; anchor 2 explicitly covers inferable budget with an unpriced privileged channel (the floorplan). Same standard as 2610.15572.

CLIP-ranked bounded key-view selection is K301-style retrieval; graph-node candidates chosen by the VLM with geometry kept in the harness fit R07 partially; discrete modes to deterministic planners fit K104. Unmet conditions are recorded per card; R07's sources do not include this paper.
